note: Official names, descriptions and grades as published on PlayStation (55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden on PlayStation until earned). Every guide below is written for this entry; each names three sources and what each source backs. Sources are cited, never copied.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.where: Everywhere — it unlocks the instant the other 54 trophies are all earned.
trophies.guide: The platinum needs no task of its own: it pops automatically when the fifty-fourth other trophy lands. The sensible order is the roadmap in this tracker — story first so nothing time-sensitive slips past, stranger strands while their givers are still around, then the counted activities and location sweeps, and the 100% completion trophy near the end because it needs almost everything else anyway. When exactly one trophy is holding the platinum back, the kind and grade filters plus the Next Up strip in this app isolate it in seconds.
steps: Work the five roadmap stages in order, ticking trophies off here as they pop.
Clear every missable-flagged trophy before the final mission.
Finish A Long Road (100% completion) last — it overlaps nearly everything else.
The platinum appears on its own the moment the count reaches 54 of 54.

Finish the fishing sequence the mission teaches you.
Reach the mission-complete screen — the trophy pops there.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.where: Anywhere you drive — ramps, rooftop gaps and clean landings across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts across the whole playthrough. Stunts are the jumps and near-miss style feats the game registers while driving — ramps, rooftop gaps and clean landings. The counter is cumulative and never resets, so the efficient route is a fast bike and a repeatable ramp loop: find one reliable jump near a respawn point and farm it, or simply drive everywhere instead of fast-travelling and let the count build during story play. Check the stats screen (and the counter in this app) to see how many you still need.
steps: Pick a fast bike and one reliable ramp you can repeat safely.
Loop the jump, landing cleanly each time — crashes do not count.
Drive instead of fast-travelling during the story to bank stunts free.
Stop at 250 on the stats screen; the silver pops on the last landing.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.where: The Shooting Range — its challenge boards, one weapon class at a time.
trophies.guide: The grind trophy of the list: gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Each challenge is a short timed target course, and gold demands near-perfect accuracy at speed. Work through them weapon by weapon, learn each course's target order, and restart the instant a run goes sloppy rather than finishing a doomed attempt. Short sessions between story missions keep it painless — a few golds a day clears the set long before the endgame, and the counter here shows exactly how many golds remain.
steps: Open a challenge and run one slow sighting attempt to learn the target order.
Restart immediately on any sloppy run — do not finish doomed attempts.
Clear one weapon class fully before moving to the next.
Repeat in short sessions until all 42 show gold.

Learn a course with one slow sighting run, then attack it — most time is lost on tight turns, so brake early and keep the line smooth. trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges — the short feat-based tasks tracked in the challenges menu (distance driven, near misses, weapon feats and similar). Open the challenges screen, sort by progress, and finish the ones you are closest to first; many complete themselves during normal play.
